messages.content: Return only JSON with keys boundary,risks,protocol,tests. Design the smallest safe Unix-domain-socket carrier over an existing long-lived NDJSON inference broker. Facts: one process must own the sole shared scheduler and append-only journal; jobs are JSON objects with globally unique IDs; results settle asynchronously; durable completed IDs replay without provider spend; queue/seen sets are bounded; EOF/SIGTERM currently drains; malformed lines are contained; one process lock excludes another journal owner. Multiple autonomous colony clients must connect without launching the broker. The socket must remain host-local, preserve per-client result isolation, survive client disconnect after admission, prevent an untrusted client from shutting down the broker, and bound line bytes/connections/write buffers. Specify the minimal wire protocol and the four highest-risk acceptance tests. Do not propose HTTP, a global work pool, or per-client schedulers.

Excludes: broker scheduler and journal internals, inference provider calls, and client-side reconnection policy.","risks":["Slow-reading client fills per-connection write buffer; broker result-delivery path blocks or leaks memory until OOM, degrading all in-flight jobs on that connection.","Two clients submit identical job IDs concurrently; without atomic seen-set insertion the broker may enqueue duplicates and double-bill the inference provider.","Incremental line-length bypass: client streams bytes without a newline, holding a grow-able read buffer indefinitely before the MAX_LINE check fires.","Connection-exhaustion DoS: untrusted clients open idle connections up to MAX_CONNS before sending any job, denying admission to legitimate submitters.","Stale socket file from a crashed broker prevents rebind; new broker must detect an unresponsive socket path, unlink it, and rebind atomically before accepting any client.","Result routing table retains a stale connection reference after client disconnect; a reconnecting client or a different client receives a pushed result intended for the original submitter."],"protocol":"One UTF-8 NDJSON line per message. Limits: MAX_LINE=65536 B, MAX_CONNS=128, MAX_WBUF=256 KiB; broker force-closes on any breach. Client→Broker: {t:\"job\",id,payload} submit; {t:\"sub\",id} fetch settled result; {t:\"ping\"} keepalive. Broker→Client: {t:\"ack\",id} admitted; {t:\"dup\",id,payload} journal replay, no provider call; {t:\"result\",id,payload} pushed to submitting connection only; {t:\"err\",id,code,msg} job failure; {t:\"reject\",code,msg} then close. Unknown t → reject+close. No shutdown, drain, or admin types exist in the protocol.","tests":["Open a connection, submit 50 jobs without reading any responses. Assert broker closes the connection once the per-client write buffer reaches MAX_WBUF, no broker OOM occurs, and a concurrently connected client continues receiving its own results uninterrupted.","Submit job ID X from client A, await {t:\"ack\"}. Before settlement, submit ID X from client B; assert B receives {t:\"ack\"} and exactly one provider call fires. Post-settlement, submit ID X from client C; assert C receives {t:\"dup\",payload} with zero provider calls.","Client A submits job X, receives {t:\"ack\"}, then closes the connection. Client B submits unrelated job Y. After both settle, assert B receives only Y result and never X; then A reconnects and sends {t:\"sub\",id:\"X\"} and receives {t:\"dup\",payload} from the journal.","Sequentially send {t:\"shutdown\"}, {t:\"drain\"}, and a 65537-byte line to a connected client. Assert each triggers {t:\"reject\"} or immediate connection close, broker PID is unchanged throughout, and a new client can connect and receive a settled result within 2 seconds."]}

structured_output.boundary: Unix-domain-socket IPC layer between the single broker process (sole journal and scheduler owner) and N colony clients. Covers: connection admission and lifecycle, NDJSON line framing with hard byte limits, per-client result push routing, and connection/buffer resource caps. Excludes: broker scheduler and journal internals, inference provider calls, and client-side reconnection policy.
risks: Slow-reading client fills per-connection write buffer; broker result-delivery path blocks or leaks memory until OOM, degrading all in-flight jobs on that connection.
Two clients submit identical job IDs concurrently; without atomic seen-set insertion the broker may enqueue duplicates and double-bill the inference provider.
Incremental line-length bypass: client streams bytes without a newline, holding a grow-able read buffer indefinitely before the MAX_LINE check fires.
Connection-exhaustion DoS: untrusted clients open idle connections up to MAX_CONNS before sending any job, denying admission to legitimate submitters.
Stale socket file from a crashed broker prevents rebind; new broker must detect an unresponsive socket path, unlink it, and rebind atomically before accepting any client.
Result routing table retains a stale connection reference after client disconnect; a reconnecting client or a different client receives a pushed result intended for the original submitter.
structured_output.protocol: One UTF-8 NDJSON line per message. Limits: MAX_LINE=65536 B, MAX_CONNS=128, MAX_WBUF=256 KiB; broker force-closes on any breach. Client→Broker: {t:"job",id,payload} submit; {t:"sub",id} fetch settled result; {t:"ping"} keepalive. Broker→Client: {t:"ack",id} admitted; {t:"dup",id,payload} journal replay, no provider call; {t:"result",id,payload} pushed to submitting connection only; {t:"err",id,code,msg} job failure; {t:"reject",code,msg} then close. Unknown t → reject+close. No shutdown, drain, or admin types exist in the protocol.
tests: Open a connection, submit 50 jobs without reading any responses. Assert broker closes the connection once the per-client write buffer reaches MAX_WBUF, no broker OOM occurs, and a concurrently connected client continues receiving its own results uninterrupted.

Submit job ID X from client A, await {t:"ack"}. Before settlement, submit ID X from client B; assert B receives {t:"ack"} and exactly one provider call fires. Post-settlement, submit ID X from client C; assert C receives {t:"dup",payload} with zero provider calls.

Client A submits job X, receives {t:"ack"}, then closes the connection. Client B submits unrelated job Y. After both settle, assert B receives only Y result and never X; then A reconnects and sends {t:"sub",id:"X"} and receives {t:"dup",payload} from the journal.

Sequentially send {t:"shutdown"}, {t:"drain"}, and a 65537-byte line to a connected client. Assert each triggers {t:"reject"} or immediate connection close, broker PID is unchanged throughout, and a new client can connect and receive a settled result within 2 seconds.
